	Let $A\in{\mathbb R}^{m\times n}$ and $\gamma\geq0$. We say $A$ is $\gamma$-nice if all of the following conditions hold.

nodes.statement: The proof of Lemma~ consists of two steps. First, we show that the primal and the dual solution pair of ideal SNN at time t is the optimal solution pair of a perturbed ell_1 minimization problem defined as shifting the b in the constraint Ax=b to Ax^ideal(t). See~ for the definition of the perturbed program. Next, by the standard perturbation theorem from optimization, we can upper bound \|x^ideal(t)\|_1 with the distance between the original program and the perturbed program. Specifically, the difference induced by the perturbation is related to the ell_2 norm of the differnce between b and Ax^ideal(t), which is exactly the residual error. As a result, we know that the difference between the optimal value of the original ell_1 minimization program and that of the perturbed program will converge to 0. Namely, we yield a convergence of \|x^ideal(t)\|_1 to OPT^ell_1. See Section~ for more details.

		$$
